title: Stefan Savage
name: Stefan Savage
summary: Computer-security researcher known for empirical studies of Internet abuse, malware ecosystems, and the security of networked systems.
whyThisMatters: Savage helped establish data-driven, ecosystem-level analysis as a core method for understanding online abuse and defensive priorities.

sections.overview:
Stefan Savage is a computer-security researcher at the University of California, San Diego. His work studies how Internet-scale systems fail and how abuse operates across technical and economic infrastructure.

Measuring abuse

Rather than treating malicious activity as isolated incidents, Savage’s research has used measurement to map relationships among malware, hosting, advertising, and payment systems. This perspective has helped security teams focus on intervention points beyond a single compromised machine.

Systems perspective

His work illustrates the value of reproducible measurement and interdisciplinary thinking in security research.

timeline.event: Begins research on networked systems and security.
Publishes widely cited work on Internet measurement, spam, and malicious online ecosystems.
Leads large-scale studies of malware distribution and the economics of cybercrime.
Continues security and systems research at UC San Diego.
